items.title: Chris Parker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 5, 2023
items.q: my friend Steve Gadd you know

ctx.x: Did it affect — did the visual art — some kind of affect the music in some fashion?

Absolutely. They’re totally entwined. And I’ve always related the two things together and sometimes I look at a painting and like let’s see for an example like a Wassily Kandinsky painting — I look at it and I say man that’s Elvin Jones to the max. You know that’s like totally how Elvin Jones would paint if he painted. Or I look at a painting — I mean I listen to a drummer like my friend Steve Gadd you know, and say man that is like photorealism you know, that’s like Chuck Close, he’s so perfect and his technique…

I was watching a video that was connected to a recent trio record and I almost had to wind back a little bit because you were using terms — you were talking about the music but it sounded like you were talking about art. And so I — it really rang a bell with me as Lester Young might have said, because I used to work in aesthetic education and we were always trying to find those connections so to hear you say that I just thought was terrific.
